chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from Fuzayl Bin Yasaar who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: Indeed, Al-Iman includes Al-Islam, and Al-Islam does not include it. Al-Iman is what settles in the hearts, and Al-Islam is that upon which are the marriages, the inheritances, and the sparing of the bloods; and Al-Iman shares/includes Al-Islam, and Al-Islam does not share/include Al-Iman.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Iman and Islam according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi articulates the Shia doctrine of 'Iman having degrees' by distinguishing between the internal reality of conviction (Iman) and the external legal status of submission (Islam). While Islam provides the framework for social and legal rights like marriage and inheritance, true Iman requires the heart's firm establishment in belief, meaning one can be a Muslim in law without possessing complete Iman. This distinction underscores the Shia emphasis on the integration of inner sincerity with outer practice, a concept central to theological debates on the nature of faith.
